title: Workshop seat holds with 10-minute expiry
scenario: Replay a hold/confirm/cancel/comp event log against workshop capacities, with 10-minute hold expiry, then report occupancy and per-attendee seats.

verified.why_correct: `left - seats >= 0` is the same as seats <= left, which is rule 2 (in use + requested at most capacity). E02 fills WS-01 exactly and is accepted, as it should be.

bugs.title: Hold age read with timedelta.seconds
bugs.why: `timedelta.seconds` is only the seconds part after whole days are taken out. zed's hold is 1 day 6 minutes old, so `.seconds` is 360 and the hold looks fresh. The late confirm succeeds, and the later cancel then finds a booking to cancel.
hints: E35 confirms a hold placed the previous afternoon. How old is it?
Look at how is_expired measures the hold's age.
probes: Why did E05 (12 minutes) still expire correctly?
Why didn't WS-07's occupancy in the report change?
bugs.symptom: test_1 test_hold_expiry: E35 is 'ok' instead of 'expired' and E36 is 'ok' instead of 'nothing_to_cancel'. E05's 12-minute expiry is still right, and the report is unchanged.

bugs.title: Event session ids upper-cased but not trimmed
bugs.why: The session ids in events.csv are only upper-cased, so E17's ' WS-09' keeps its leading space and doesn't match the trimmed key from sessions.csv. It is reported as unknown_session instead of full. The mixed-case ids still match, which hides the problem.
hints: E17 says unknown_session, but WS-09 exists. Look at the raw row.
Compare how session ids are cleaned in load_sessions and in load_events.
probes: Why did ws-01 and ws-05 events work even with this change?
Why did no occupancy number change?
bugs.symptom: test_1 test_rejection_reasons: E17 is 'unknown_session' instead of 'full'. Everything else matches.

bugs.title: Cancelled bookings counted in attendee seats
bugs.why: `b.status == "confirmed" or "comped"` parses as `(b.status == "confirmed") or "comped"`, and the non-empty string is always truthy, so every booking counts, including dev's cancelled 3 seats.
hints: Look at the status filter in attendee_seats.
probes: Why are the session `taken` numbers still right?
bugs.symptom: test_2 test_attendee_seats: an extra 'dev@lab.io': 3 entry (dev cancelled that booking). Session occupancy is unaffected.

context_qa.q: How does replay() process the events?
context_qa.a: It builds a `Ledger` from the sessions and calls `ledger.apply(ev)` for each event in file order. `apply` checks unknown session and `closed` first, then dispatches to `hold`, `confirm`, `cancel` or `comp` by the action name and stores the outcome in `ledger.outcomes`.

context_qa.q: Where are holds stored, and when are they removed?
context_qa.a: `Ledger.holds` is a dict keyed by `(session_id, attendee)`. `confirm` pops the hold for its key, and `cancel` pops it if there is no active booking. Expired holds aren't deleted on their own; `held()` and `hold()` call `is_expired` to skip them.
The seats of bookings for that session whose status is in `OCCUPYING` (`confirmed`, `comped`). Holds are counted separately by `held()`.

context_qa.q: How are ids cleaned on load?
context_qa.a: `load_sessions` keys sessions by `norm_session` (trim + upper). `load_events` sets `action` and `attendee` with `clean(...).lower()` and builds `session_id` from the row on the `session_id=` line. A blank seats cell becomes 1.
It takes `now - hold.held_at` (a timedelta), converts it to a number of seconds and checks whether that is greater than `HOLD_SECONDS` (600).

context_qa.q: What feeds the attendees section of the report?
context_qa.a: `attendee_seats(ledger.bookings)`, which loops over all bookings (including cancelled ones), applies a status condition and sums seats per attendee into a Counter, returned as a sorted dict.
